rationale: PatchArena uses the 'fresh' recovery policy when step 7 (diff collection and safety scan) fails. The pipeline attempts sandbox deletion in its finally block, including the tested success, exception, timeout, and cancellation paths. Local tests cover these paths, but they do not prove successful deletion under every possible live failure condition. Because git operations at step 7 are trusted application commands, a failure here (e.g. git diff timeout or filesystem error) does not necessarily imply corrupted agent state that needs snapshot restoration. The cost of discarding the sandbox is low: the candidate is marked FAILED and no further work can usefully be done. A rollback to a pre-patch snapshot would require Celesto snapshot support verified against the installed CLI version, which was not tested in this implementation. The fresh policy is the selected recovery strategy; the implementation attempts deletion under asyncio.shield to reduce cancellation-related interruption, and records cleanup results in the failure trace. This does not guarantee that every deletion succeeds. The limitation versus rollback is that intermediate work products may be lost, which is acceptable because a failed candidate is not promoted to winner.
